questions.question: Where are stop lines painted?
questions.explanation: Stop lines are white lines painted across traffic lanes. They show drivers exactly where to stop at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign warns that a traffic signal is coming. Be ready to stop for a yellow or red light.

questions.question: Drivers cannot pass from either side of a ____ centerline.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: When a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line mark the road with the broken line next to your lane, you may pass if:
questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is on your side, you may pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming. Watch for vehicles crossing your path.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Slow down and go through the intersection.
Stop, then go when the way is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
You can turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop and stay stopped. Wait for a green light or green arrow before going.

questions.question: What should you remember when driving on wet pavement?

options.text: The road is especially slippery right after rain starts.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are dangerous and slippery, especially right after rain starts. Your tires can lose grip on the wet surface. This can cause hydroplaning. Slow down and leave more distance between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: Alcohol-related crashes cause what percent of deaths in car crashes?
questions.explanation: Alcohol-related crashes cause 29 percent of all deaths in car crashes. Driving while drunk is a serious problem.

questions.question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move ahead or fall back so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move ahead or fall back so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in another driver's blind spot. Speed up or slow down so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: Which offense will automatically suspend your license?

options.text: Leaving the scene of an accident without helping

questions.explanation: Your license can be automatically suspended for certain offenses. These include driving while intoxicated, leaving an accident scene, and driving with an invalid license.

questions.question: Emergency vehicles:

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.
Can use a loudspeaker to give instructions.

questions.explanation: You must yield to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or air horns with red or blue flashing lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only proceed when you are sure the way is clear.

questions.question: On long trips, you can prevent drowsiness by:

options.text: Stopping at regular intervals for a rest.
Moving your eyes from side to side as you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping at regular intervals for a rest.
questions.explanation: To prevent drowsiness on long trips, stop regularly to rest and stretch. Do this even if you don't feel tired.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know that:

options.text: Vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
You must give pedestrians in crosswalks the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians are responsible for staying out of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must give pedestrians in crosswalks the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show where pedestrians can safely cross. Lines can be horizontal, vertical, or both. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, you should expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing the street.
Run out in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and use extra caution near children. They may not understand danger and may run into the street without looking.

questions.question: You notice a vehicle defect that may affect safe operation. You should:

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you can afford it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any defect that affects safe operation as soon as possible. Do not drive the vehicle until it is fixed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This one-way sign means traffic moves only in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: When a vehicle is entering your freeway lane from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn so they know you are there.
Ignore them because you have the right-of-way.
Change lanes or slow down to give them room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down to give them room.
questions.explanation: Make room for vehicles entering the freeway. Change lanes when possible to let them merge safely. If you cannot change lanes, slow down.

questions.question: You have the right-of-way when turning left with which traffic signal?
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go in the direction the arrow points. Oncoming traffic must stop for you to turn.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, with or without a crosswalk.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street, you must:

options.text: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until it passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or a siren approaches on a one-way street, drive to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill grade is coming.

questions.question: How many seconds should you stay behind a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Any contact between a car and motorcycle can injure the rider. Keep four to six seconds between you and a motorcycle. This gives the rider time to turn or stop if needed.

questions.question: It is illegal to follow a fire truck with its siren on closer than ____ feet.
questions.explanation: You must stay at least 500 feet away from a fire truck responding to a call. Do not drive or park within the block where a fire truck has stopped.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve because few cars come from the other direction.
By driving on the highway shoulder.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the other lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or curves—you cannot see oncoming cars and might crash. Never drive on the shoulder to pass. Do not cross solid yellow lines to pass.

questions.question: Which medications can make driving unsafe?
questions.explanation: Any medication can affect your driving. Ask your doctor or pharmacist about side effects. Read labels on over-the-counter medicines to check if they impair driving.

questions.question: For drivers 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol level of:
questions.explanation: Adults cannot drive with a blood alcohol level of 0.08 percent or higher. Drunk driving is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect a driver?
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows reaction time and affects judgment. It impairs coordination and balance. Your vision and ability to judge distance worsen after drinking, making it hard to react to what's around you.

questions.question: When slowing on a slippery road, what should you do first?
questions.explanation: First, take your foot off the gas. If you need to slow more, gently press the brake pedal with steady pressure.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic at a school, you must:

options.text: Follow what other cars do, not the guard.
Assume the guard should not be there.
Drive as if no children are present.

questions.explanation: Always follow a crossing guard's directions in a school zone. Slow down and be extra careful around schools.

questions.question: You can only pass safely on a two-lane, two-way street if:

options.text: You can see far enough ahead.
You can get back before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your car is fast enough to pass.

questions.explanation: You can pass safely only if you can see ahead clearly, return to your lane before oncoming cars arrive, and your vehicle can go fast enough to pass. Never pass where it is illegal or unsafe.
